cards.explanation: The answer is to walk worthy of their calling. Paul, an apostle writing to the believers in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1), says, “…I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received…” He writes this as a prisoner, and he calls himself an ambassador in chains (Ephesians 6:20). I think that gives his words extra weight, friends. A man in chains is asking about the walk, not the view.

Humility and gentleness are on Paul's list. Verse 2 opens it with “…all humility and gentleness…” Those two come first, and patience follows. Friends, humble and gentle sounds quiet, but a gentle person in a heated moment is the loudest thing in the room. That's a worthy walk.

The answer is True. Right after humility and gentleness, Paul writes “with patience.” It's one of the things he lists for a worthy walk. Patience is the one I have to practice every time a batch is in the oven and my mustache itches to open the door.

The answer is the unity of the Spirit. Paul says, “…with diligence to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.” Notice he says preserve, friends. The unity is already there, and the job is to guard it with diligence. It's like a fresh batch cooling on the rack: you don't have to make it again, you just have to keep hands and elbows off it.
The answer is False. Paul says the unity of the Spirit is kept “…through the bond of peace.” Strict rules don't show up anywhere in that verse, friends. Peace is what holds it together.

The answer is one hope. Paul says, “There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called…” One hope, friends. Everybody in the body is headed toward the same one. That means nobody has to hunt for their own.

The answer is over all and through all and in all. Paul describes the one God and Father of all as the One “…who is over all and through all and in all.” Over, through and in, friends. Three little words, and I find them comforting.

The answer is each one of us. Paul says, “Now to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.” Each one, friends. Paul counts himself in that "us," and a stamper from the back of a junk drawer happily does too.

The answer is to fill all things. Paul says the One who descended is the very One who ascended above all the heavens, “…in order to fill all things.” So going up had a purpose, and the purpose was filling. Friends, I think of it like a bakery with the oven on. The warmth reaches every corner.

The answer is apostles and prophets. Verse 11 says, “And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers…” So apostles and prophets are the first two on the list. Evangelists, pastors and teachers follow right behind them, friends.

The word is equip. Paul says He gave them “…to equip the saints for works of ministry…” Equip means getting people ready to do the work. A good leader hands you the tools and then trusts your hands to use them.

The answer is True. Verse 12 says they're given “…to equip the saints for works of ministry and to build up the body of Christ…” Equipping and building up go together in the same sentence, friends. The body of Christ is what's being built.

The answer is False. Paul says it continues “…until we all reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God, as we mature to the full measure of the stature of Christ.” Leaders aren't a stopping point, friends. The goal is much bigger than a headcount.

The word is infants. Paul says, “Then we will no longer be infants, tossed about by the waves and carried around by every wind of teaching…” He's talking about growing up into maturity. I'll say it plain, friends: nobody's embarrassed to have been an infant once. The point is to keep growing.

The answer is False. Paul describes believers who aren't mature as “…tossed about by the waves and carried around by every wind of teaching…” He also mentions “…the clever cunning of men in their deceitful scheming.” He never calls any of it harmless, friends.

The answer is the truth in love. Paul says, “Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will in all things grow up into Christ Himself, who is the head.” Paul puts truth and love together in one phrase, friends. Speaking the truth is the job, and love is how he says to do it.

The word is head. Paul says we grow up into Christ Himself, “…who is the head.” The body grows up into the head. I think that's a picture worth keeping, friends, since everything else in the body takes its direction from the head.

The answer is the work of each individual part. Paul says the whole body “…grows and builds itself up in love through the work of each individual part.” Each part, friends, not just a few. I'm just a small stamper, and I'd say that's good news.
